section_summary.extract_value: This section explores the relationship between creativity and intelligence, particularly focusing on the CHC theory's constructs of Long-term storage and retrieval (Glr), Fluid Reasoning (Gf), and Crystallized Knowledge (Gc). The 'present study' (Study X) involved 116 participants and investigated the link between Glr and creativity using subtests from the Kaufman Assessment Battery for Children–II and Kaufman Test of Educational Achievement – II Brief, alongside multiple creativity measures including self-assessments and rated creative performance in drawing and writing. The findings indicated Glr was significantly related to creative drawing but not creative writing or most self-assessed creativity measures. The section also reviews prior research, including a meta-analysis by Kim (2005) and studies by Silvia, Beaty, and Nusbaum (2013) and Benedek, Könen, and Neubauer (2012), which examined correlations between intelligence aspects and creativity.
